name: JWT, OAuth, secrets, and SSRF hardening for Python services
short_definition: Auth and security baseline for FastAPI Python services: verify JWTs with explicit algorithms and required claims (PyJWT), prefer Supabase/Auth issuer JWTs or service-to-service tokens over homemade sessions, never trust client roles, keep secrets in env/secret manager via pydantic-settings, and treat server-side URL fetch as SSRF-critical. Aligns with Next cookie SSR (backend-auth) — Python receives Bearer or service credentials, not browser cookie jars by default. As of 2026-07-13: PyJWT 2.13.0, cryptography 49.0.0, authlib 1.7.2, bcrypt 5.0.0.
scope_in: Bearer JWT verification (HS256 service secrets vs RS256/ES256 JWKS)
FastAPI Depends current_user / APIRouter dependencies for authZ
OAuth2 password/bearer patterns and Authlib when acting as OAuth client
Password hashing if local users exist (bcrypt/argon2 — rare if Supabase owns identity)
scope_out: Full CSP/HTML XSS product surface (backend-security.md for Next UI)

defaults.identity_source: Supabase Auth (or IdP) issues JWT; Python verifies signature + claims
defaults.library: PyJWT (pyjwt) + cryptography; avoid python-jose for greenfield
defaults.algorithms: Explicit algorithms=[...] on every decode; never verify with algorithms accepting 'none'
defaults.claims: require exp, sub; validate aud and iss when issuer is known; leeway small (≤60s)
defaults.authz: After authN, check resource ownership/role server-side; JWT role claim is hint not sole gate for sensitive ops
defaults.di: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]; router-level dependencies on /v1 protected prefixes
defaults.secrets: pydantic-settings; SecretStr; never log secrets; rotate JWT signing keys with kid
defaults.passwords: If needed: argon2-cffi or bcrypt; never roll crypto; prefer IdP owns passwords
defaults.ssrf: Allowlist hosts; block private/link-local/metadata IPs; https only; redirects rechecked

use_jwt_bearer_when: Python service is called by Next BFF, mobile, or other services with tokens
Supabase JWT or internal RS256 service tokens available
use_api_key_when: Machine webhooks / simple service keys with rotation (still rate limit + constant-time compare)
do_not: Don't invent cookie session stack in Python when Next already owns SSR sessions
Don't accept getSession-equivalent untrusted payloads without verify
Don't put long-lived secrets in frontend or OpenAPI examples

alternatives.supabase_py: When calling Supabase with user JWT for RLS-scoped data

do: jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["RS256"], audience=..., issuer=..., options={"require": ["exp", "sub"]})
Fetch JWKS with cache + kid rotation; pin expected issuer URL
Return 401 for missing/invalid auth; 403 for authenticated but forbidden
Separate authN dependency from authZ helpers (require_role, require_owner)
Strip sensitive fields from error bodies in production
dont: Don't use algorithms=None or accept alg from token header alone (alg confusion)
Don't use HS256 with a public/guessable secret; don't share HS256 secret with browsers
Don't trust role from body/query; don't authorize only in middleware without route checks
Don't log Authorization headers or full JWTs
Don't disable aud/iss checks 'to make it work' in prod
Don't fetch user URLs server-side without SSRF allowlist

code_skeleton:
from typing import Annotated, Any

import jwt
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    jwt_secret: str  # HS256 dev only; prod prefer RS256 + JWKS
    jwt_audience: str = "authenticated"
    jwt_issuer: str = "https://PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1"

settings = Settings()  # from env
security = HTTPBearer(auto_error=True)
app = FastAPI()

class User(BaseModel):
    sub: str
    role: str | None = None
    claims: dict[str, Any]

async def get_current_user(
    creds: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(security)],
) -> User:
    token = creds.credentials
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token,
            settings.jwt_secret,
            algorithms=["HS256"],  # replace with RS256 + jwk client in prod
            audience=settings.jwt_audience,
            issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
            options={"require": ["exp", "sub"]},
        )
    except jwt.PyJWTError as e:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid token",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        ) from e
    return User(sub=str(payload["sub"]), role=payload.get("role"), claims=payload)

CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)]

@app.get("/v1/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"sub": user.sub}

# SSRF sketch
ALLOWED_HOSTS = frozenset({"api.openai.com", "api.anthropic.com"})

def assert_public_https_url(url: str) -> None:
    from urllib.parse import urlparse
    p = urlparse(url)
    if p.scheme != "https" or p.hostname not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="URL not allowed")
failure_modes: Alg confusion / missing algorithms= allow forged tokens
Clock skew: valid tokens rejected (no small leeway) or expired accepted (huge leeway)
JWKS not refreshed → outage after IdP key rotation
Service role key used in user request path → privilege escalation
AuthZ only on some routes → IDOR on forgotten handlers
SSRF to cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) via connector features
CORS * with credentials reflecting tokens to evil origins
anti_patterns: JWT in localStorage patterns copied into Python OpenAPI clients as default
decode without verify signature (options verify_signature False) in prod
OAuth state/nonce omitted when implementing authorization code client

avoid_greenfield: passlib as sole modern default without care

deprecation_watch: HS256 shared secret shipped to any client code
getSession-style trust without server verify (TS anti-pattern mirrored in Python)
OAuth implicit flow for new apps
ts_boundary: Next owns browser session cookies via @supabase/ssr. Python services should accept Authorization: Bearer <access_token> from BFF or mobile, verify JWT, and enforce authZ. Do not re-implement cookie SSR in Python for the same app. Service-to-service: separate audience/issuer or mTLS. Align claim names (sub, role) with Supabase JWT custom claims.
rust_boundary: Rust extractors for JWT when edge gateway is Axum; same verify rules (explicit alg, aud, iss). Prefer one verification library policy per trust domain; don't dual-verify differently in Python and Rust for the same token type without tests.
supabase_boundary: User JWT → RLS-scoped DB access; service_role only for admin jobs, never exposed. Prefer getUser-equivalent validation for sensitive mutations (introspect/Auth API) when revoke must be immediate; pure JWT verify is fine for low-risk read paths with short exp. Custom claims for roles when table lookup is too slow — still re-check on privilege changes.
boundary_contracts: Bearer JWT scheme in OpenAPI securitySchemes
Webhook paths use signature verify not user JWT

decision_matrix_row.python: PyJWT verify + Depends authZ; Supabase/IdP issued tokens
decision_matrix_row.rust: JWT/API key extractors on hot gateways

threats: Privilege escalation via role claim tampering or missing ownership checks
Secret exfiltration from logs, traces, OpenAPI, error dumps
Token replay after logout if only local JWT verify and long exp
CSRF less relevant for pure Bearer APIs; still care if cookie auth added
mitigations: Short access token TTL + refresh at IdP; denylist/version claim for critical revoke
Secret manager + gitleaks; SecretStr; redaction filters
URL allowlists and network egress policies for SSRF

must_generate: HTTPBearer + Depends get_current_user with jwt.decode algorithms list

tests_required: Valid token → 200; expired → 401; wrong aud → 401; wrong sig → 401
API key compare timing-safe unit test
SSRF allowlist rejects private IPs and bad schemes

No python-jose greenfield; no verify_signature False
